9700               	;
9701               	; 	' THE SIXTEENTH-PIXEL ACCUMULATOR. hx is one unsigned byte per screen
9702               	; 	' (2), so there is nowhere to keep a fraction -- the fraction lives here
9703               	; 	' and is spent as whole pixels. THREE IFs, not a loop and not a divide:
9704               	; 	' `%` and `/` both compile to a real TMS9900 DIV (CLAUDE.md 3A) and this
9705               	; 	' runs every pass.
9706               	; 	'
9707               	; 	' THE NUMBER OF DRAINS IS A CEILING ON THE SPEED, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE
9708               	; 	' POINT OF THIS COMMENT. Each IF can spend one whole pixel, so N drains
9709               	; 	' cap hspd at N px per pass NO MATTER WHAT hsp64 SAYS. The invariant is:
9710               	; 	'
9711               	; 	'     hacc is under 16 on entry, and hsp64 is at most 48,
9712               	; 	'     so hacc is under 64 here and three drains always suffice.
9713               	; 	'
9714               	; 	' KEEP hsp64 <= 48. This was quarter-pixels with TWO drains and the same
9715               	; 	' invariant written the same way -- "hsp4 is at most 8, so it can never
9716               	; 	' need a third" -- and it was correct until somebody set hsp4 = 9 without
9717               	; 	' re-reading it. The crook then ran at a flat 2.0 px/pass while every
9718               	; 	' comment, the design table and assets/checkchase.py all said 2.25, and
9719               	; 	' the surplus quarter leaked into hacc and wrapped the byte every 256
9720               	; 	' passes. Nothing failed; he simply arrived two thirds of a screen short
9721               	; 	' of his own escape. checkchase.py now counts these IFs and refuses a
9722               	; 	' speed the drains cannot deliver.
9723               	; 	'
9724               	; 	' 7, NOT 6, AND THE REASON IS MEASURED. Tracked off the reference video
9725               	; 	' (DESIGN.md 4a), the 2600's Kelly covers 0.40 screen widths a second and
9726               	; 	' its Harry 0.193 -- a ratio of 2.07. At hsp4 = 6 ours was 2.67, and the
9727               	; 	' crook visibly strolled. 7 brings it to 2.29. 8 would match the original
9728               	; 	' exactly and cannot be used: Kelly's route here is 1.95x Harry's, so a
9729               	; 	' speed ratio of 2.0 leaves the on-foot chase 0.2 s of slack, which is no
9730               	; 	' chase at all. checkchase.py holds the line.
9731               	; 	' STILL RUNNING FROM THE STAIRS -- and this has to come BEFORE the move,

9831               	;
9832               	; 	' HE WALKS BY REAL TIME, NOT BY LOOP PASS -- one accumulate-and-drain per
9833               	; 	' ELAPSED FRAME rather than per pass. Everything that moves here used to be
9834               	; 	' per pass while the CLOCK is paced by the frame delta, so a busy screen
9835               	; 	' slowed Harry in real seconds and the clock did not slow with him: the
9836               	; 	' same uninterrupted escape finished with nine timer units in hand from a
9837               	; 	' light screen and none at all from the lift screen, decided by where the
9838               	; 	' player happened to be standing. Now he covers the same ground per second
9839               	; 	' wherever anybody is (DESIGN.md 0f-ter).
9840               	; 	'
9841               	; 	' A LOOP, NOT A MULTIPLY. `*` compiles to a real TMS9900 MPY, and reading a
9842               	; 	' 16-bit variable straight after one returns the product's HIGH word
9843               	; 	' (CLAUDE.md 3A). fdv is 1..3 here, so this is at most three adds.
9844               	; 	'
9845               	; 	' SIXTY-FOURTHS, AND ONLY TWO DRAINS -- both fall out of accumulating per
9846               	; 	' FRAME instead of per pass. He covers under a pixel a frame, so two drains
9847               	; 	' are ample where the per-pass version needed three; and the finer unit is
9848               	; 	' what makes the speed tunable at all. In sixteenths one step was about six
9849               	; 	' SECONDS of his route, so nothing landed near the buzzer; in sixty-fourths
9850               	; 	' it is about one and a half. Keep hsp64 <= 128: hacc is under 64 on entry,
9851               	; 	' so 64 + 128 stays inside a byte and two drains always suffice.
9852               	; 	'
9853               	; 	' AND THE STEP IS CLAMPED TO THREE FRAMES' WORTH, WHICH IS NOT A DETAIL.
9854               	; 	' Two tests sample his position once a pass and neither interpolates:
9855               	; 	'
9856               	; 	'   ARRIVAL   `hdx < 6` around the escalator or the roof door -- an ELEVEN
9857               	; 	'             pixel window. A step over 10 px can jump clean across it and
9858               	; 	'             he never arrives at all.
9859               	; 	'   THE CATCH `hdd < CATCHR` is 12, a 23-wide band, and Kelly closes 4 of
9860               	; 	'             it himself -- so Harry over ~18 px could pass through the Kop
9861               	; 	'             between two passes without either sample being inside it.
9862               	; 	'
9863               	; 	' The clamp and the drains live in pace_step now, with the reasoning; the
9864               	; 	' numbers above are what sized them. Measured: TIME 02 on the lift screen
9865               	; 	' against TIME 04 on a light one when the clamp was 3, and 00 against 09
9866               	; 	' before any of this.
9867               	; 	'
9868               	; 	' The ESCALATOR RIDE is deliberately untouched: it returns above this,
9869               	; 	' clocked one step per pass to stay locked to the moving staircase. A rider
9870               	; 	' advanced by the frame delta either drifts off the treads or makes the
9871               	; 	' steps run backwards (CLAUDE.md 3A, DESIGN.md 0f). It is about 3% of his
9872               	; 	' journey.
9873               	; 	'
9874               	; 	' `hanim` still advances by hspd and is still an ODOMETER -- pixels
9875               	; 	' travelled, not time -- so the run cycle stays locked to the ground at any
9876               	; 	' rate. A 9 px step moves it exactly one pose of its 8 px beat.
9877               	; 	pacc = hacc

10337               	;
10338               	; 	' ======================================================================
10339               	; 	' COLLISIONS -- pure arithmetic against RAM, no VDP reads
10340               	; 	' ======================================================================
10341               	; 	' Kelly's box is [kfh, kfh + kh) above the slab; an obstacle's is
10342               	; 	' [ohb, oht). The ball's inset hitbox is what makes 8..10 avoidable both
10343               	; 	' ways -- without it there is a height at which the ball can be neither
10344               	; 	' jumped nor ducked, and an unavoidable hazard is not difficulty.
10345               	; 	' ONE HIT PER CONTACT, WITH A REFRACTORY PERIOD.
10346               	; 	'
10347               	; 	' The overlap test is true on every frame the player is touching
10348               	; 	' something, so with no latch at all one clumsy cart charges nine seconds
10349               	; 	' several times over -- and what the player sees is the clock jumping by
10350               	; 	' 27, from which the only available conclusion is that the penalty is
10351               	; 	' broken.
10352               	; 	'
10353               	; 	' A latch that clears on the first non-overlapping frame is still not
10354               	; 	' enough, and the case that breaks it is the BOUNCING BALL: it rises off
10355               	; 	' the player between bounces, which is a genuine loss of contact, so a
10356               	; 	' player standing still under one is taxed on every single bounce while
10357               	; 	' being given no opportunity to do anything about it. Technically two
10358               	; 	' collisions; in play, one situation.
10359               	; 	'
10360               	; 	' So obht() is a countdown, not a flag. A hit sets it to HITREF; it ticks
10361               	; 	' down only while the player is CLEAR, and the same obstacle cannot charge
10362               	; 	' again until it reaches zero. Contact holds the count up, so parking
10363               	; 	' inside something never earns a second penalty either.
10364               	; coll_obst:
10365               cvb_COLL_OBST

10686               	; 	' THE FLOOR CLEARS WHEN YOU ARE HIT, and stays clear until you re-enter
10687               	; 	' the screen. Nine seconds is a heavy penalty on a fifty-unit clock, and
10688               	; 	' taking it while still standing among the things that charged it -- with
10689               	; 	' a second hazard 48 px behind the first -- is how one mistake becomes
10690               	; 	' three. Clearing the row makes the penalty a single event you can walk
10691               	; 	' away from.
10692               	; 	'
10693               	; 	' BOTH SLOTS, WHATEVER IS IN THEM. Radios used to be exempt: they are
10694               	; 	' CHARACTERS stamped into the name table rather than sprites, so zeroing
10695               	; 	' the kind would have stopped them colliding while leaving them plainly
10696               	; 	' visible on the shelf, and a fixture that is still there has to still be
10697               	; 	' there. That was a reason to UNDRAW them, not a reason to keep them --
10698               	; 	' and it left the one hazard that cannot leave on its own as the only one
10699               	; 	' the mercy did not cover. haz_off now takes the characters with it.
10700               	; 	'
10701               	; 	' NOTHING RESTORES IT HERE. load_band repopulates the band from the
10702               	; 	' template, and it runs only on a seam crossing or a round start, so
10703               	; 	' "until the screen is re-entered" costs no state and no timer: leave and
10704               	; 	' come back and the hazards are simply placed again.
10705               	; 	'
10706               	; 	' THE CALL ITSELF IS IN THE MAIN LOOP, at the end of the freeze -- see
10707               	; 	' the hfz block there for why.
10708               	; 	' A HIT DOES NOT END A JUMP. This used to force ST_RUN and zero the arc,

10875               	; 	' AND THEY HAVE TO BE AT THE SAME HEIGHT, NOT MERELY ON THE SAME FLOOR.
10876               	; 	'
10877               	; 	' `hlv` does not change until a ride ENDS -- a crook stepping onto a
10878               	; 	' flight keeps the floor he left until he arrives at the next one. So
10879               	; 	' while he was most of a storey up or down the stairs he still counted as
10880               	; 	' standing on the floor he started from, and a Kop who ran over the head
10881               	; 	' of the flight arrested him through the floor. Reported from play:
10882               	; 	' "I run over top of him, even though we do not touch".
10883               	; 	'
10884               	; 	' It is the same shape of bug as the catch that fired at MAXIMUM
10885               	; 	' separation: a test that is right about one axis and silent about the
10886               	; 	' other, where the silent one happens to be true nearly all the time.
10887               	; 	'
10888               	; 	' UNSIGNED-SAFE. Riding up is above the shared floor and riding down is
10889               	; 	' below it, which is a signed quantity, and CVBasic's variables are not.
10890               	; 	' So both are collected as POSITIVE heights on opposite sides -- Kelly's
10891               	; 	' climb plus Harry's descent on one side, Harry's climb on the other --
10892               	; 	' and the difference is taken between two numbers that cannot go
10893               	; 	' negative. Two riders passing on the same flight measure the sum of
10894               	; 	' their heights, which is exactly the distance between them.
10895               	; 	hva = 0
10896 E310 04C0  14 	clr r0
10897 E312 D800  38 	movb r0,@cvb_HVA
     E314 21E9

11000               	; 	' RIDING WITH THE DOORS SHUT: HIDE HIM AND DO NOT DRAW HIM AT ALL.
11001               	; 	'
11002               	; 	' This test used to sit AFTER his sprites had been written, so every pass
11003               	; 	' placed him at his old floor and then hid him again. That is not free.
11004               	; 	' CVBasic's SPRITE writes a RAM mirror which the vblank ISR copies to
11005               	; 	' VRAM, so a vblank landing BETWEEN the draw and the hide latches the
11006               	; 	' visible state for a frame -- and draw_actors is long (Kelly, Harry,
11007               	; 	' eight obstacles) while a pass on the lift screen spans two or three
11008               	; 	' frames, so it happened constantly. He flickered at the floor he had
11009               	; 	' just left, which reads as a drawing bug rather than as a journey.
11010               	; 	'
11011               	; 	' Deciding BEFORE drawing costs one test and cannot race the ISR at all:
11012               	; 	' the mirror never holds a position to be caught with.
11013               	; 	IF klst = ST_ELEV THEN

11078               	; 	' the highest-numbered sprites on an over-full scanline, so the lowest
11079               	; 	' slots are the ones that can never disappear, and the player is the one
11080               	; 	' thing that must never disappear.

11086               	; 	' cost just as much as a full one. Two actors meeting is four, exactly

11233               	; 		' FOUR RUN FRAMES FROM TWO BITS of the animation counter, and no
11234               	; 		' divide -- `/` compiles to a real TMS9900 DIV (CLAUDE.md 3A) and
11235               	; 		' this is per-frame code. Two adjacent bits give 0,4,8,12.
11236               	; 		'
11237               	; 		' KELLY USES BITS 2 AND 3 AND HARRY USES 3 AND 4, because a stride
11238               	; 		' has to cover about a stride's worth of ground or the figure
11239               	; 		' skates. Kelly runs 4 px a frame, so four frames a pose is 16 px;
11240               	; 		' Harry runs 1.75, so eight frames a pose is 14. Matching the two
11241               	; 		' rates to the two speeds is what keeps both looking like running.
11242               	; 		kq = P_KLEG1

11606               	; 	' HE RISES A PIXEL ON THE RECOVERY BEATS. A runner is highest at mid-flight
11607               	; 	' and lowest at contact; with the body pinned at a constant y, alternating
11608               	; 	' legs under a motionless torso reads as a dance rather than as travel.
11609               	; 	'
11610               	; 	' One pixel is enough at this size, and it lifts the BODY ONLY -- the legs
11611               	; 	' keep their y, so the planted foot stays on the floor and the figure
11612               	; 	' stretches at the waist instead of hopping. Lifting the legs too would be
11613               	; 	' a jump.
11614               	; 	'
11615               	; 	' Beats 2 and 4 are the recoveries, which is exactly `hanim AND 8` -- the
11616               	; 	' cycle's LOW beat bit. IT MUST MOVE WITH THE BEAT BITS ABOVE IT: on the
11617               	; 	' wrong bit he rises and falls twice per stride, a second clock inside one
11618               	; 	' figure, which is the flapping of DESIGN.md 0j2 in the vertical.
11619               	; 	'
11620               	; 	' Safe because HARRY'S COLLISION HAS NO VERTICAL COMPONENT: he is caught on
11621               	; 	' `same level AND |dx| < CATCHR`. Doing this to Kelly would desynchronise
11622               	; 	' his sprite from the ball and biplane windows in DESIGN.md 5a, which is

11626               	; 	'

11629               	; 	'   * Lifting the body alone opens a one-pixel gap at the waist, and the
11630               	; 	'     torso's bottom row and the legs' top row do not align across it --
11631               	; 	'     green shows through and he reads as coming apart.
11632               	; 	'
11633               	; 	' It also keeps `hfy = hy - 7` and `hy2 = hy + 16` LITERAL, which is not a

11635               	; 	' parsing those exact expressions. Bobbing a differently-named variable

11638               	; 	' THE RECOVERY LIFT IS A RUNNING THING. Standing on a step he would

12117               	;
12118               	; 	' ======================================================================
12119               	; 	' THE SCANNER
12120               	; 	' ======================================================================
12121               	; 	' Rows 21-23, 16 chars wide, centred: 48 characters whose PATTERNS are
12122               	; 	' poked directly, so a moving dot costs two writes and no name-table
12123               	; 	' traffic. With the flip (DESIGN.md 2a) this is how you know where Harry
12124               	; 	' is at all -- he can be one pixel off-screen and completely invisible.
12125               	; 	'
12126               	; 	' Rows 21-23 all sit in the THIRD screen third, so every scanner pattern
12127               	; 	' is at base 4096 and no third-selection arithmetic is needed.
12128               	; 	'
12129               	; 	' BOTH DOTS ARE WHITE and Kelly's BLINKS. The manual wants Kelly black
12130               	; 	' and Harry white, but this is the TMS9918's two-colours-per-8x1-cell
12131               	; 	' mode: a black dot and a white dot on the same pixel row of the same
12132               	; 	' character cannot both exist. Blinking distinguishes them with one
12133               	; 	' colour, which is what RallyX does with its player dot.
12134               	; 	' THE STEPS MOVE, AND EVERY ESCALATOR ON SCREEN MOVES WITH THEM. A flight
12135               	; 	' is twelve characters -- six per direction, sliced out of a rendered
12136               	; 	' 64x40 bitmap by genart.py -- so rewriting those twelve PATTERNS animates
12137               	; 	' the lot: 96 bytes, no name-table traffic, and the same cost whether one
12138               	; 	' flight is visible or ten. The phases slide the cells ALONG the slope, so
12139               	; 	' the steps travel up the flight rather than drifting sideways.
12140               	; esc_tick:
12141               cvb_ESC_TICK
12142               	; 	' ONLY SCREENS 0 AND 7 CARRY A FLIGHT, so six screens in eight skip this
12143               	; 	' entirely -- which is what makes rewriting the cells every frame
12144               	; 	' affordable. Nested, not `klsc > 0 AND klsc < 7`: the 9900 backend
12145               	; 	' miscompiles a compare-AND-compare (CLAUDE.md 3A).
12146               	; 	IF klsc > 0 THEN

12165               	; 	' ONE PHASE PER PASS, AND NEVER MORE. There are four phases covering an
12166               	; 	' 8 px period, so advancing by the frame delta ALIASES: at fdv 2 the
12167               	; 	' pattern flips between two positions half a period apart and the
12168               	; 	' direction stops being readable, and at fdv 3 the sequence runs 0,3,2,1
12169               	; 	' -- the staircase visibly runs BACKWARDS, carrying its steps down while
12170               	; 	' the rider goes up. That is the wagon-wheel effect, and no amount of
12171               	; 	' phase arithmetic fixes it: a 4-phase cycle can only be stepped by 1.
12172               	; 	'
12173               	; 	' So the ANIMATION is the clock here, and the rider is paced from it --
12174               	; 	' see move_kelly, which advances him by the same fixed 2-and-1 per pass
12175               	; 	' rather than by fdv. Locking the two together is the only way they
12176               	; 	' cannot drift, and it is what "the player moves at the rate the steps
12177               	; 	' carry him" actually means. The cost is that a ride takes 36 passes
12178               	; 	' rather than 36 frames, so it slows down when the loop does -- which is
12179               	; 	' the honest behaviour for a machine that is carrying you.

12477               	; 	' ------------------------------------------------- the scanner's furniture
12478               	; 	' Without this the scanner is two dots in a void: you can see THAT Harry is
12479               	; 	' somewhere, but not what he is near, which is the one thing you actually
12480               	; 	' need when he is off-screen. Floor lines say which level, the slashes say
12481               	; 	' where that floor's escalator is, and the bar says where the elevator is --
12482               	; 	' exactly the three things the manual lists.
12483               	; 	'
12484               	; 	' FURNITURE AND DOTS ARE SEGREGATED BY PIXEL ROW ON PURPOSE, and a level
12485               	; 	' band is now FOUR rows, one per colour, because a pixel row carries
12486               	; 	' exactly one colour here:
12487               	; 	'
12488               	; 	'   +0  GREY    escalator head, and the elevator car
12489               	; 	'   +1  GREY    the air of that floor
12490               	; 	'   +2  GREY
12491               	; 	'   +3  YELLOW  the floor line -- and NOTHING else goes here
12492               	; 	'
12493               	; 	' THE FIRST THREE ROWS ARE THE FLOOR'S AIR AND EVERYTHING LIVES IN THEM:
12494               	; 	' the escalator's three-step diagonal, the lift car, and both actors, all
12495               	; 	' three pixels tall. They are grey in the table, and the Kop and the
12496               	; 	' crook recolour their own CHARACTER as they move (scan_mark) -- which is
12497               	; 	' what lets both of them fill the band instead of getting a pixel row
12498               	; 	' each. Eight pixels of this canvas is half a screen of the store, so
12499               	; 	' they are almost never in one character; when they are, they merge.
12500               	; 	'
12501               	; 	' Shrinking from six rows bought eight empty pixel rows, four above the
12502               	; 	' instrument and four below, so it no longer butts against the shop floor

12849               	;
12850               	; 	' Blank the canvas by WRITING zeros rather than copying 384 of them out
12851               	; 	' of ROM. This runs twice a game -- at setup and on a new Krook -- so a
12852               	; 	' loop costs nothing anybody can perceive, and it hands the fixed area
12853               	; 	' back the best part of half a kilobyte, which is the budget that
12854               	; 	' actually binds. Paced in bursts: a few hundred VDP writes in a single
12855               	; 	' frame are silently dropped (CLAUDE.md 3A).
12856               	; scan_wipe:
12857               cvb_SCAN_WIPE
12858               	; 	' THIS ADDRESS IS A CHARACTER CODE IN DISGUISE, AND IT WENT STALE.
12859               	; 	' 4096 is the pattern table's BOTTOM THIRD -- rows 16-23, which is
12860               	; 	' band 0 and the radar together -- and the canvas characters begin at
12861               	; 	' genart's SCAN_FIRST, so the base is 4096 + SCAN_FIRST*8. It was
12862               	; 	' written out by hand as 4096 + 160*8 when SCAN_FIRST was 160; art
12863               	; 	' added later moved SCAN_FIRST to 208 and nothing moved this with it,
12864               	; 	' so the wipe zeroed the 48 characters BELOW the canvas and never
12865               	; 	' touched the canvas at all.
12866               	; 	'
12867               	; 	' Two of those forty-eight are STRUCTURE. ENDWALL is the building's
12868               	; 	' outside wall and SLABP is a pillar's cap. Blanking a pattern in ONE
12869               	; 	' THIRD leaves a character that draws correctly everywhere else and
12870               	; 	' falls back to its own background colour here -- so the GROUND FLOOR's
12871               	; 	' outside wall turned into plain green while the identical wall one
12872               	; 	' storey up was perfect, and the ground floor's pillars lost the brick
12873               	; 	' carried up through the bar above them. ENDWALL appears only on
12874               	; 	' screens 0 and 7, which is exactly why it was reported as happening
12875               	; 	' only on the escalator screens, mirrored side to side.
12876               	; 	'
12877               	; 	' The name table was correct the whole time. Probing it said so, four
12878               	; 	' times. It was the GLYPH that was empty, in one third only -- which a
12879               	; 	' probe that copies the character somewhere else to look at it cannot
12880               	; 	' see, because the copy renders from a different third's pattern.
12881               	; 	'
12882               	; 	' renumber.py rewrites this line from genart.SCAN_FIRST, and
12883               	; 	' checkstruct.py fails the build if the two disagree.

12953               	; 	' THE TWO ACTORS ARE SPRITES; EVERYTHING ELSE IS CHARACTERS.
12954               	; 	'
12955               	; 	' That split is what makes the instrument simple. The floor lines, the
12956               	; 	' flights and the lift car do not move relative to the canvas, so they
12957               	; 	' are pixels in the scanner's own characters and cost nothing to keep.
12958               	; 	' The Kop and the crook DO move, and as sprites they need no colour
12959               	; 	' table, no erase and no priority arithmetic -- they draw over the
12960               	; 	' furniture because sprites always do, and nothing shifts to make room.
12961               	; 	'
12962               	; 	' IT ALSO REMOVED THE BLINK. Kelly flashed because a pixel row of this
12963               	; 	' canvas can only carry one colour, so at close range the two markers
12964               	; 	' merged and the blink was the only thing left to tell them apart. Two
12965               	; 	' sprites are two colours wherever they stand.
12966               	; 	'
12967               	; 	' The furniture is drawn ONCE, by scan_furn. It used to be redrawn every
12968               	; 	' tick because erasing a character-based marker ANDed bits out of
12969               	; 	' whatever it was standing on; there is nothing left to rub it away. The
12970               	; 	' car still redraws itself, because the car actually moves.
12971               	; 	' -- the lift car. IT WAS FLICKERING, and the cause was not the drawing
12972               	; 	' but the ERASING: scan_elev cleared its three cells and put them back
12973               	; 	' every tick, whether or not the car had moved, so several times a second
12974               	; 	' there was a window with the pixels off. A sprite has no erase at all --
12975               	; 	' it is placed, and the VDP does the rest -- and slot 26 sits BELOW the
12976               	; 	' two markers, so the Kop and the crook pass over it without either of

13761               	;
13762               	; 	' THE BONUS IS COUNTED OUT, NOT AWARDED. Dropping the whole sum into the
13763               	; 	' score in one frame tells the player a number; ticking the clock down a
13764               	; 	' unit at a time, with the score climbing and a beat under each step,
13765               	; 	' tells them what the number was FOR. It is the pay-off for every second
13766               	; 	' they saved, and every arcade game of this era spends a moment on it.
13767               	; 	'
13768               	; 	' It also costs nothing to get right: the loop already has to run down
13769               	; 	' `tsec`, so the animation IS the calculation, and the repeated-addition
13770               	; 	' note below stops applying -- each step adds one band's worth.
13771               	; 	'
13772               	; 	' x100 for Krooks 1-9, x200 for 10-15, x300 from 16. Two independent
13773               	; 	' sources agree on those bands; the manual's own wording suggests
13774               	; 	' 1-8 / 9-16 / 17+ and DESIGN.md 0 records the disagreement.
13775               	; 	'
13776               	; 	' IN UNITS OF TEN, WHICH IS WHAT THE SCORE IS COUNTED IN, so the bands are
13777               	; 	' 10 / 20 / 30 and not 100 / 200 / 300.
13778               	; 	'
13779               	; 	' They were 100 / 200 / 300 and paid TEN TIMES the right bonus -- 1,000 a
13780               	; 	' time unit where the original pays 100. `add_score` takes `#addv` in units
13781               	; 	' of ten (the prize beside it is `#addv = 5` for fifty points, and the bonus
13782               	; 	' Kop threshold is `#nextk = 1000` for ten thousand), so writing the band in
13783               	; 	' POINTS here shifted every tally one decimal place. Reported from play as
13784               	; 	' "it seems like you awarded 1000 per time unit left" -- exactly right.
13785               	; 	'
13786               	; 	' Nothing failed: 1,000 a unit is a plausible-looking number, the digits
13787               	; 	' all line up, and the only symptom is a score that runs away. The tell is
13788               	; 	' a constant written in a different unit from the routine it is passed to,
13789               	; 	' which is the same class of fault as the px-per-pass speeds in 3A.
13790               	; 	'
13791               	; 	' (This is also why the old comment here said "#bval MUST BE 16-BIT: 300
13792               	; 	' does not fit in a byte". At 10 / 20 / 30 it would, but it stays 16-bit
13793               	; 	' because `#addv` is, and a byte here would buy two bytes of ROM in
13794               	; 	' exchange for a truncation trap the next time somebody edits a band.)
13795               	; bonus_count:

13911               	;
13912               	; 	' AND IT ENDS ON ITS LAST BLIP -- there is no closing accent.
13913               	; 	'
13914               	; 	' Two were tried. The bench's own ending for this variant rose a fourth,
13915               	; 	' to 2,542 Hz, and a square wave there is a shriek -- the same fault the
13916               	; 	' pickup was rewritten for. Dropping it an OCTAVE BELOW the ticks, to
13917               	; 	' 518 Hz, was reported the same way, and that one cannot be too high by
13918               	; 	' any measure: it is the lowest note in the effect.
13919               	; 	'
13920               	; 	' So the complaint is not the pitch, it is the extra note. A tally is
13921               	; 	' arithmetic, and arithmetic finishes when the last term is added; a
13922               	; 	' flourish after it is a second event the player has to interpret, and
13923               	; 	' the HUD has already said the clock is empty. The count stops when the
13924               	; 	' counting stops.
13925               	;
13926               	; 	' `calc_bonus` USED TO LIVE HERE and computed the whole sum by repeated
13927               	; 	' addition, to dodge two hazards at once: `tsec * bmul` is an 8-bit
13928               	; 	' product (a 50-unit capture in the x300 band pays 15,000, six times past
13929               	; 	' a byte), and multiplying properly lands on the MPY/r0 hazard where a
13930               	; 	' 16-bit variable read straight after being multiplied returns the
13931               	; 	' product's high word. Counting the bonus out a unit at a time (above)
13932               	; 	' removes the multiply entirely rather than working around it -- the loop
13933               	; 	' the player watches IS the arithmetic.
13934               	; 	'
13935               	; 	' It also fixed the last-tick case for free: `bn_loop` tests `tsec = 0`
13936               	; 	' on entry, where the old `FOR bi = 1 TO tsec` would have run its body
13937               	; 	' once and paid a full multiplier for no time at all (CLAUDE.md 3A).
13938               	;

14237               	;
14238               	; 	' A SOUND STILL PLAYING WHEN THE ROUND ENDS IS ALLOWED TO FINISH.
14239               	; 	'
14240               	; 	' This used to open with a bare `GOSUB snd_off`, which cut it dead. That
14241               	; 	' was not an accident: the decay counters are ticked by the MAIN LOOP, and
14242               	; 	' this pause REPLACES the main loop, so a tone left latched with nothing
14243               	; 	' ticking it hangs for the full ninety frames -- the sticky-audio failure
14244               	; 	' this game has already shipped twice. The answer is to DRAIN the counters
14245               	; 	' rather than to stop silencing.
14246               	; 	'
14247               	; 	' CLEAR THE PENDING LATCHES FIRST. sf* flags are sounds that have not
14248               	; 	' happened yet; left set, the drain below would START one and the pause
14249               	; 	' would end with a fresh note ringing into the next round.
14250               	; 	'
14251               	; 	' THEN TICK sfx_tick WHOLE, not some decay-only part of it. The five
14252               	; 	' counters do not all live in one place: sot, sht and spt are a block at
14253               	; 	' the tail, but spz (the prize arpeggio) and swt (the jump warble) tick up
14254               	; 	' among the code that starts sounds. Draining only the tail would finish a
14255               	; 	' footstep and still cut the arpeggio, which is the one effect with a
14256               	; 	' phrase worth saving. Calling the whole routine also leaves the write
14257               	; 	' order on CHANNEL 2 alone, which spz and spt share.
14258               	; 	'
14259               	; 	' EVERY THIRD FRAME, because the main loop runs about 2.5 frames per pass
14260               	; 	' and this loop waits one frame per turn. Ticking every frame would play
14261               	; 	' everything at two and a half times its tuned speed. Three frames a tick
14262               	; 	' is ~17% slow and gives 30 ticks against the longest effect's 20 passes.
14263               	; 	'
14264               	; 	' THE LOOP COUNTS TICKS, NOT FRAMES, which is what makes the pacing free.
14265               	; 	' Counting 91 frames and firing on every third needs a second counter, an
14266               	; 	' increment and a test -- 48 bytes, on a fixed area with 66 left. Counting
14267               	; 	' 31 TICKS of three WAITs each is the same 93 frames and the same three
14268               	; 	' frames per tick, with none of that. The duration changes by two frames.
14269               	; 	'
14270               	; 	' snd_off still runs at the END, as the backstop for anything the drain
14271               	; 	' did not finish.
14272               	; pause_beat:
14273               cvb_PAUSE_BEAT

14635               	;
14636               	; 	' THE LOW-TIME WARNING IS SILENT. There was a beep a second under ten, and
14637               	; 	' it was the wrong instrument for the job: the last ten seconds are the
14638               	; 	' busiest part of a round, so a repeating tone arrives exactly when the
14639               	; 	' player most needs to hear the hazards, and it fought the prize arpeggio
14640               	; 	' for channel 2 as well. The flash says the same thing and says it in the
14641               	; 	' place the player is already looking.
14642               	;
14643               	; 	' FOOTSTEPS ARE NOISE, AND ON THE NOISE CHANNEL -- testsounds variant A.
14644               	; 	'
14645               	; 	' They were two alternating TONES on channel 0, which is neither what the
14646               	; 	' original does nor a good use of a channel: the recording says a footstep
14647               	; 	' is a short burst of white noise, and channel 3 was sitting unused while
14648               	; 	' the footsteps and the jump sweep shared channel 0 and had to take turns.
14649               	; 	'
14650               	; 	' TESTSOUNDS RUN D: a SHORT tick at the measured RATE.
14651               	; 	'
14652               	; 	' The two dials are independent and both were tried at the bench. The
14653               	; 	' 2600 plays a 64 ms burst every 165 ms -- six a second -- and variant A
14654               	; 	' copies both. Ten a second was tried on the way here and reads as
14655               	; 	' hurrying rather than running. What D changes is not the cadence but the
14656               	; 	' TICK: two frames rather than four, and a notch louder to carry at half
14657               	; 	' the length. Same six a second, less of it.
14658               	; 	'
14659               	; 	' EIGHT A SECOND, AND THE ACCUMULATOR NOW CARRIES ITS REMAINDER.
14660               	; 	'
14661               	; 	' sfw counted pixels and the trigger did `sfw = 0`, THROWING AWAY whatever
14662               	; 	' was past the threshold. kspd is about four pixels a pass, so a threshold
14663               	; 	' of 17 did not fire at 17 -- it fired at the first multiple past it, about
14664               	; 	' 20, and every rate this was ever set to came out slower than the number
14665               	; 	' said: the "six a second" was 5.2 and the "ten" that read as hurrying was
14666               	; 	' really 8.7. Subtracting the threshold instead keeps the fraction, so the
14667               	; 	' rate is what it claims to be at any walking speed.
14668               	; 	'
14669               	; 	' MEASURED OFF THE COLECOVISION: 14 px, about 7.4 a second.
14670               	; 	'
14671               	; 	' It was 15 px and 6.9 a second, picked between an 8.0 that read as
14672               	; 	' slightly hurried and a 6.1 that read as trudging -- a judgement between
14673               	; 	' two other judgements, with nothing underneath it. The ColecoVision
14674               	; 	' recording settles it: footfalls land every 0.130 s across a twelve-second
14675               	; 	' continuous run, which is 7.7 a second, and that is the one finding in the
14676               	; 	' whole sound analysis the method resolves EXACTLY -- a rhythm rather than a
14677               	; 	' pitch, counted off the RMS track rather than inferred from a spectrum.
14678               	; 	' (colecosounds variant 1A; assets/sfx/sfxref-coleco.md has the working.)
14679               	; 	'
14680               	; 	' 104 px/s over 14 px is 7.43 a second. 13 px would give 8.00, and 7.7 sits
14681               	; 	' almost exactly between them -- so this is the nearer of the two, and it is
14682               	; 	' also the one that does not walk back into the 8.0 that was rejected by ear.
14683               	; 	'
14684               	; 	' WHY THE GAME KEEPS A DISTANCE AND THE BENCH KEEPS A CADENCE. The bench
14685               	; 	' plays a fixed eight frames between steps because it has no walking to tie
14686               	; 	' them to; the game accumulates PIXELS TRAVELLED, so the feet keep time with
14687               	; 	' the legs when he is slowed or stopped. Matching "7.4 a second" therefore
14688               	; 	' means matching it AT HIS WALKING SPEED, and assumes the ColecoVision's
14689               	; 	' crook walks at ours -- which the recording cannot confirm.
14690               	; 	'
14691               	; 	' The dial is this one constant and the subtraction below, which must stay
14692               	; 	' threshold + 1 or the carry is wrong.
14693               	; 	'
14694               	; 	' SOT = 2 IS THE SHORTEST TICK THERE IS, and 1 is SILENCE. The decay block
14695               	; 	' below runs LATER IN THE SAME sfx_tick, so a count of 1 is decremented to
14696               	; 	' zero on the pass that set it and the note-off fires before the sound has
14697               	; 	' lasted any time at all. 2 survives to the next pass, which is one pass of
14698               	; 	' sound -- about 42 ms against the bench's 33, as close as a per-pass timer
14699               	; 	' gets, and the reason the bench and the game cannot sound identical.
14700               	; 	'
14701               	; 	' Register 4 is white noise at the fastest rate.
14702               	; 	'
14703               	; 	' VOLUME 9, WHICH IS UNDER EVERYTHING ELSE ON PURPOSE. The hit, the prize
14704               	; 	' and the jump are 12 and 13, and they happen ONCE; footsteps play for the
14705               	; 	' whole round. At 13 they were level with the events they are supposed to
14706               	; 	' sit beneath, so the effects that carry information had nothing to stand
14707               	; 	' out from. The tone version was 7 for the same reason -- noise does read
14708               	; 	' quieter than a tone at the same number, which is why this is 9 and not

14906 FEB0 C03A  30 	mov *r10+,r0
14907 FEB2 0450  20 	b *r0
14908               	;
14909               	; 	' EVERYTHING BELOW THIS LINE IS ASSEMBLED INTO BANK 1, so the INCLUDE order
14910               	; 	' is load-bearing and nothing but data may follow it.
14911               	; 	'
14912               	; 	' THE FONT IS NOW IN THE BANK TOO, and it used to be deliberately outside:
14913               	; 	' keeping one readable thing in bank 0 means a bank-selection mistake shows
14914               	; 	' as "text survives, art does not" rather than a uniformly blank screen,
14915               	; 	' which is a genuinely useful thing to have when a bank goes wrong.
14916               	; 	'
14917               	; 	' THE FONT HAS A BANK OF ITS OWN, and the reason is not its size.
14918               	; 	'
14919               	; 	' Bank 1 was FULL -- six spare bytes of 8,192 -- which shut the door on
14920               	; 	' moving anything else out of the fixed area, and the fixed area is the
14921               	; 	' only budget that cannot be grown (linkticart writes exactly three
14922               	; 	' loader pages and discards the rest; they are the 32K expansion's RAM at
14923               	; 	' >A000, not cart ROM). A second bank costs a bigger cart -- five pages
14924               	; 	' round up to eight, so 32 KB becomes 64 KB -- and buys back the ability
14925               	; 	' to keep evacuating data out of code.
14926               	; 	'
14927               	; 	' THE FONT IS THE RIGHT TENANT because it is read ONCE. Two DEFINEs copy
14928               	; 	' it into VRAM at setup and nothing looks at it again, so it is the only
14929               	; 	' block here that can sit on a page which is not permanently mapped. See
14930               	; 	' setup_font: bank 2 is selected for those two statements and bank 1 for
14931               	; 	' the whole of the rest of the program.
14932               	; 	'
14933               	; 	' EVERYTHING ELSE STAYS IN BANK 1, because everything else is read during
14934               	; 	' play -- art on a screen crossing, templates on a band blit, the lookup
14935               	; 	' tables every pass. One permanently-mapped bank for all of it means
14936               	; 	' there is no switch to miss.
14937               	; 	#if TI994A
14938               	; 	BANK 2
14939      014A     BANK_0_FREE:	EQU >fffe-$

15077               	;
15078               	; 	' THE COLOUR TABLE, 472 bytes of the same value ($14 = black ink on dark blue).
15079               	; 	'
15080               	; 	' Loaded with DEFINE COLOR 32,59,font_col, which is ONE synchronous call that
15081               	; 	' writes all three screen thirds (define_color always does the LDIRVM3 triple
15082               	; 	' copy). It replaced a VPOKE loop that wrote this one value 1,416 times paced by
15083               	; 	' 24 WAITs -- the largest scripted delay in the boot, and the reason the title
15084               	; 	' screen used to fill in visibly rather than appearing at once.
15085               	; 	'
15086               	; 	' EIGHT BYTES PER CHARACTER, not one. Supply fewer and DEFINE COLOR reads
15087               	; 	' whatever follows in ROM as colour data, with no error at build or run time.
15088               	;
15089               	; font_col:
15090               cvb_FONT_COL

15603               	; 	INCLUDE "art.bas"
15604               	; 	' Keystone Kapers art -- GENERATED by assets/genart.py. Do not edit; regenerate.
15605               	; 	'
15606               	; 	' EVERY SPRITE IS 16x16: sprite size and magnification are GLOBAL on the
15607               	; 	' TMS9918, so small objects are drawn small INSIDE a 16x16 box rather than
15608               	; 	' being small sprites.
15609               	; 	'
15610               	; 	' EVERY 8-PX OBJECT SITS IN ROWS 8-15 OF ITS BOX, ducked Kelly included, so
15611               	; 	' one rule places them all: bottom edge = y + 16, and a thing resting on the
15612               	; 	' floor is at y = FLOORY - 16.
15613               	; 	'
15614               	; 	' Sprite bytes are QUADRANT-ORDERED: 16 rows of the left half, then 16 of
15615               	; 	' the right. Every block is an EVEN number of bytes -- an odd DATA BYTE run
15616               	; 	' silently misaligns every word table after it (CLAUDE.md 3A).
15617               	;
15618               	; spr_kelly:	' Kelly: RIGHT hat/face/tunic/tunic-arm-up/duck-hat/duck-face, then the same LEFT (+24), then the FOUR shared run frames. Patterns 0..60
15619               cvb_SPR_KELLY

     626A 0000     
     626C 0000     
     626E 0000

16875               	; 	INCLUDE "store.bas"
16876               	; 	' Keystone Kapers store -- GENERATED by assets/genstore.py. Do not edit.
16877               	; 	'
16878               	; 	' EIGHT band templates of 5 rows x 32 cols (160 bytes each) plus a 32-byte
16879               	; 	' index over (level, screen). The whole 8-screen, 4-level building is about
16880               	; 	' 1.3 KB instead of the 5,120 bytes it would cost to store literally.
16881               	; 	'
16882               	; 	' All eight templates are ONE contiguous block under ONE label, so a band
16883               	; 	' blit is
16884               	; 	'     SCREEN stor_tpl, tpl*160, toprow*32, 32, 5, 32
16885               	; 	' with no label ladder -- SCREEN needs a literal label and a label cannot be
16886               	; 	' chosen by a variable, which is why RallyX needed a 4-way IF over its maze
16887               	; 	' tables. One block sidesteps it.
16888               	; 	'
16889               	; 	' 160 is EVEN, so this cannot leave the location counter odd and misalign
16890               	; 	' the word tables defined after it.
16891               	; 	'
16892               	; 	' template ids:
16893               	; 	'   0 T_AISLE_A
16894               	; 	'   1 T_AISLE_B
16895               	; 	'   2 T_ESC_W
16896               	; 	'   3 T_ESC_E
16897               	; 	'   4 T_ELEV
16898               	; 	'   5 T_ROOF0
16899               	; 	'   6 T_ROOF1
16900               	; 	'   7 T_ROOF2
16901               	; 	'   8 T_ROOF3
16902               	; 	'   9 T_ROOF4
16903               	; 	'   10 T_ROOF5
16904               	; 	'   11 T_ROOF6
16905               	; 	'   12 T_ROOF7
16906               	; 	'   13 T_END_W
16907               	; 	'   14 T_END_E
16908               	;
